title: Guideline-compliant use of albumin - a multicenter retrospective status quo analysis
summary: Albumin is an expensive and time-consuming drug due to documentation. It is also produced from human blood and should therefore be used sparingly. There are guidelines for the use of albumin, which specify the diseases for which albumin should be used. Based on internal experience from community clinics, it can be concluded that human albumin is sometimes not used in compliance with these guidelines. The aim of this study is to investigate how often albumin is used in accordance with these guidelines. For this purpose, files in the participating clinics are analyzed retrospectively. There will be no patient contact or intervention in ongoing therapies.
conditions: Analysis of the active substance albumin according to ATC B05AA01

interventions.name: For patients who received albumin in 2023, it will be assessed whether the administration of albumin was in compliance with guidelines.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient in the above-mentioned clinics in the period of the year 2023; patient has received at least one dose of albumin during the study period
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years
